title: Staggered capture coordinator: micro-quiesce protocol for multi-stream CUDA graph safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight coordinator and micro-quiesce protocol that staggers CUDA graph captures across concurrent decode streams to eliminate interleaved-kernel races and improve replay correctness. The coordinator does not centralize decoding — it elects a transient capture leader per CUDA device per capture-epoch, aligns prefill boundaries, and applies kernel-selection hints based on observed occupancy and sequence-length histograms. The goal is to reduce capture-related nondeterminism while preserving throughput and low P99 latency for short interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic replay pass rate >= 99.95% on the multi-stream synthetic harness (1000 concurrent streams, mixed sequence lengths 16/64/256)
No measurable regression in median latency (<2% change) on our evening traffic production test (region: us-west-2) compared to baseline runtime-1.19
Capture leader election completes within configured quiesce window (default 2ms) under 95th percentile of device occupancy
Fallback path (sequential capture per stream) is exercised automatically if coordinator detects capture-fence violations; fallback logs are surfaced in Console trace with actionable tags
Kernel hint propagation results in at least one measurable decrease in kernel selection thrash (defined as kernel-selection flips per token) vs. baseline
design_decisions: Use a quorum-free leader election per device: the first stream to reach prefill boundary sets a short device-scoped capture token; other streams back off by micro-quiesce and attach to the same capture token when compatible
Keep coordinator stateless across requests; state lives in a compact capture token embedded in the request context to avoid cross-device RPCs
Enforce a strict alignment check for KV cache epochs before sharing a capture token. Misaligned epochs trigger a soft-fallback that serializes capture for the misaligned streams
Kernel hinting is advisory: runtime may still override hints if occupancy or quantization constraints require a specific kernel path
Expose two knobs in runtime config: quiesce_window_ms and capture_backoff_factor to tune contention vs latency trade-offs
implementation_notes: Add device-capture token struct (opaque 64-bit) with epoch, leader_stream_id, and kernel_hint bits — keep size <= 64b to minimize wire cost
Instrument capture path with capture-token attach/detach events; emit perf counters for leader-election latency, token-attach failures, and fallback triggers
Modify prefill scheduling to align KV ranges when token attach succeeds — this avoids partial-KV captures that previously caused replay drift
Integrate kernel-hint scorer that consumes sequence-length histogram + quantization profile to suggest a preferred kernel family (fused-attn vs. split-attn) and preferred occupancy target
Implement fallback path: if token attach fails repeatedly, switch to per-stream sequential capture mode with an aggressive telemetry tag to identify hotspots
Add config gating: feature disabled by default on dedicated clusters until canary metrics validated; opt-in via runtime flag: runtime.enable_staggered_capture
testing_plan: Unit tests for token serialization and leader-election timeout behavior
Harness: extend multi-stream fuzz harness to introduce random prefill offsets and KV misalignment scenarios; run 10k fuzz iterations nightly
Perf evaluation: compare throughput and P50/P95/P99 latency for workloads (chat short/long, completion short/long) between baseline and feature-on in staging cluster
Determinism tests: run deterministic-replay verifier across model matrix (Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B) and quantization modes (fp16, 4bit)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: unit/integration tests + internal canary in our perf lab (single GPU node) — target 1 week
Stage 1: closed canary on dedicated sandbox region (small percent of traffic, runtime flag on) — monitor determinism and rollback triggers
Stage 2: broader canary on hosted API with traffic shaping to low-risk customers; increase traffic in 10% increments with 24h guardrails
Stage 3: enable by default for non-critical regions once 48h of stable metrics; enable on Dedicated with opt-in per-customer until enterprise sign-off

2025-02-21 Design review: decided to keep token stateless and embedded in request context to avoid additional control plane RPCs. Trade-off: slightly larger request metadata vs simpler failure modes.

2025-03-02 Perf gate: Staging run vs baseline: throughput +1.9% for short chat workload, median latency +0.8% (within target), deterministic replay failures reduced from 0.6% to 0.03% on synthetic harness.
